title: Noise-Resilient Point-wise Anomaly Detection in Time Series Using Weak Segment Labels

problem.claim: Point-level anomaly predictions are needed when training data combines segment-level labels with unlabeled data.

gap.claim: There is a substantial information gap between available segment-level or missing labels and the desired point-level targets.

contributions.claim: NRdetector is a noise-resilient framework combining confidence-based sample selection, robust segment-level learning, and data-centric point-level detection for multivariate time series anomaly detection.
The framework includes a loss function intended to mitigate label noise while incorporating temporal features.
The loss function encourages smoothness between consecutive points and separability between points from differently labeled segments.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the loss function as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world multivariate time series datasets used 11 evaluation metrics.
The authors report that NRdetector consistently achieved robust results across multiple real-world datasets.
The authors report that NRdetector outperformed various baselines adapted to the stated setting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Anomaly detection in temporal data is motivated by real-world applications involving unusual events and potential hazards.
Practical data may contain segment-level labels and unlabeled events, although the desired outputs are point-level predictions.
The mismatch between available labels and point-level targets creates a substantial information gap.
NRdetector addresses the setting with noise-resilient selection, segment-level learning, point-level detection, and a temporal loss function.
The authors report broad evaluation across real-world datasets and metrics with improved performance over adapted baselines.

source_observation.claim: The method combines confidence-based sample selection with loss design that models temporal smoothness and label-based separability.

interpretation.claim: When supervision is coarse and noisy, jointly filtering examples and encoding temporal structure may help bridge the label-resolution gap.

application.claim: This pattern may be considered for time-series tasks where weak segment annotations must support finer-grained predictions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which components are necessary or whether the approach transfers beyond the evaluated multivariate time-series setting.

unknowns: Dataset identities, sizes, and label characteristics are unspecified.
The loss function, model architecture, training procedure, and baseline configurations are unspecified.
Per-dataset results, metric definitions, and statistical comparisons are unspecified.
